summary.text: Carol Miller is the incumbent U.S. Representative for West Virginia's 1st District, seeking re-election in 2026. A real estate manager and bison farm owner, she served in the West Virginia House of Delegates before her election to Congress in 2018, and she serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means. Her official biography lists her focus as jobs, economic diversification, trade, rural health care access and the state's energy industries.

paragraphs.text: Miller was born in Columbus, Ohio, on November 4, 1950, and graduated from Bexley High School in 1968; she is the daughter of Ohio Congressman Samuel L. Devine.
She earned a B.S. in political science and history from Columbia College in 1972.
She owns and operates Swann Ridge Bison Farm and manages real estate in Huntington, West Virginia.
Miller lost a 2004 bid for the West Virginia House of Delegates, then won a seat in 2006 by defeating a Democratic incumbent.
She served in the House of Delegates until 2018, representing the 15th District and later the 16th District after redistricting, and became the first female Majority Whip in the chamber (2017-2018).

She won the 2018 Republican primary for West Virginia's 3rd District and defeated Democrat Richard Ojeda in the general election, then was re-elected in 2020. After West Virginia lost a seat in the 2020 census, she won the redrawn 1st District in 2022 and was re-elected in 2024.

In Congress, Miller serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, on its Trade and Health subcommittees; her earlier committee assignments included Oversight and Government Reform and Transportation and Infrastructure (2019-2020).
Her official page lists membership in caucuses including the Congressional Coal Caucus, Congressional Energy Export Caucus, Congressional Appalachian Caucus and Bipartisan Rural Health Caucus.
According to her official biography, she is married to Matt Miller, is a mother of two and grandmother of seven, and lives in Huntington.
